title: Bed bug treatment
subtitle: From Mitch's answers 6 Nov 2026, plus official health department notes where he said to look it up. Items marked in orange are still to confirm.
source: Mitch's answers 6 Nov 2026; LPC Tech Onboarding Pack (PPE for bed bug work, never list, what you can quote); jobbook-data/chemicals.json (Bed Bug Treatment products); jobbook-data/services.json (past wordings); Garrards technical advisory note on bedbug management found in the treatment history files; researched, not from Mitch: Victorian Department of Health Pesticide Safety Technical Notes 18 (bed bugs) and 19 (fleas), SA Health bird mites fact sheet, NSW Health bed bugs page, healthdirect bed bugs page, AEPMA Code of Practice for the Control of Bed Bug Infestations in Australia (4th edition)

sections.heading: When this job comes up
body: Customer thinks they have bed bugs. Mitch's service is called Bed Bug Treatment. Past invoices read: "Bed Bug Inspection" (with a report provided), "Bedbug Treatment x 1 room", "Bedbug Treatment x 2 rooms", and an inspection and treatment of a vehicle.
How big a bed bug job is depends on the job. There is no fixed rule by room or by house.
A vehicle is treated the same way as a room.
A written Bed Bug Inspection report is only given if the customer asks for one.
A bed bug job is one visit. A follow-up visit is quoted separately. [Mitch to confirm: can a tech quote bed bug work, or does Mitch?]
The job process, the never list, PPE and the free service period are in the Every job guide. [Mitch to confirm: does the free service period apply to this job?]

sections.heading: PPE
sections.title: PPE on before you go in
sections.note: Never apply chemicals without PPE. If the SDS requires it, you wear it. No exceptions.
items: Gloves and closed shoes at minimum
Gloves, mask and eye protection for any spray, as per the product SDS

items.text: Coveralls, gloves and mask on before you go in
items.detail: Change them before you go into the next property.

sections.heading: Before you arrive
sections.title: What the customer does before you get there
items: Strip the beds

items.detail: Linen, bedding and washable clothes. The official note says wash above 60°C and tumble dry on hot for at least 30 minutes. [Mitch to confirm: the temperature and time are from Victorian Department of Health Pesticide Safety Technical Note 18 (Bed Bugs, June 2022), not from Mitch]

items.text: Clear the floor and move furniture if they can
items.detail: [Mitch to confirm: do you ask for this, or only the strip and hot wash?]

sections.heading: Bed bugs, fleas or mites?
sections.title: Bites alone can't tell you which it is. Find the bug or the marks it leaves. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Department of Health Technical Notes 18 and 19 and the SA Health bird mites fact sheet, not from Mitch]
rows: Flat and oval, light brown, red after a feed. Up to about 5 mm, like an apple seed.
Brown and oval, 2 to 4 mm. They jump.
Under 1 mm, eight legs, very mobile. Clear until they feed, then red to black.
Exposed skin like arms and shoulders. Sometimes in rows. Some people only react 9 to 14 days later.
Legs and feet. Red swollen lump within half an hour.
No favourite spot on the body. Itchy, swollen, raised red spots.
Mattress seams, bedhead, bedside furniture, skirting.
Near bird nests (eaves, roof space, wall cavities). They move inside after the young birds leave.
Blood spots on sheets, dark spotting, shed skins, eggs. A sweet musty smell when there are lots.
Flea dirt: tiny dark specks that leave a red ring on damp white tissue.
Mites crawling on walls, ceilings and bedding.

sections.heading: Products Mitch uses
sections.title: Names as in Mitch's product list. No rates here: follow the label. Mitch uses these as the job needs, and bifenthrin as well. [Mitch to confirm: which bifenthrin product for bed bugs, Country Bifenthrin 100 Low Odour or Aquastar 100SC]
rows: Bifenthrin (Mitch also uses it for bed bugs)
Power spray rig (as listed for the bifenthrin products)

sections.heading: Where bed bugs hide
sections.title: From a Garrards advisory note in Mitch's files. Mitch's own rule is to search and treat whatever is accessible. [Mitch to confirm: do the note's steps (2 to 3 metres, take furniture apart, wrap the mattress) match how you work?]
rows: Find every harbourage within 2 to 3 metres of the bed. A harbourage is any crack you can slide the corner of a piece of paper into.
Wrap in black plastic and put it in the hot sun.
Screw it off the wall, treat behind it, put it back, seal the edges.
Take it apart, treat, put it back together, seal the gaps.
Check the curtain rails too. May need to come down and be cleaned.
Timber tongue-in-groove: get rid of the cracks.
Take it out and put it in the sun, or fumigate it. Otherwise don't put it back for three months. Liquid and dust can't treat it properly.

sections.heading: Steps
sections.title: Steps
items: Ask the customer to show you the rooms and beds with the problem
Check the beds are stripped and everything is going through a hot wash
Coveralls, gloves and mask on before you go in
Take BEFORE photos

items.detail: The bed and everything near it. The Garrards note lists dots of blood on the sheets, a sickly sweet smell, and dried blood in cracks around the bed, bedhead, bedside furniture and mattress.

items.text: Treat what you find and can get to
items.detail: Demand Duo spray, Coopex dust or bifenthrin, as the job needs. Treat the cracks and hiding spots you find. Don't space spray, the fine mist can make bed bugs scatter to other rooms. Dust suits cracks and voids. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Department of Health Pesticide Safety Technical Note 18 (Bed Bugs, June 2022), not from Mitch]

items.text: Mattress: use the approved chemical Mitch has
items.detail: Read the label first, some products can't go on mattresses. [Mitch to confirm: which product do you use on mattresses? It is not in the products table. The label check is from Victorian Department of Health Pesticide Safety Technical Note 18 (Bed Bugs, June 2022), not from Mitch]

items.text: Apply per the product label. Never exceed label rates
items.detail: Never mix chemicals without checking the label first. If in doubt, call Mitch.

items: Keep chemicals away from food, children and pets
Note anything you could not treat or reach, and why
Take AFTER photos

items.text: Tell the customer to leave the room alone for a bit
items.detail: They can go back in once it has dried. Follow the product label. [Mitch to confirm: how long is a bit, and does it mean no vacuuming or cleaning?]

items.text: Before you go into the next property, change your coveralls, gloves and mask
items.detail: Bed bugs travel on luggage, shoes and clothing. The industry code says to put worn clothing and used disposable gear in sealed plastic bags and keep equipment in sealed containers. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Department of Health Pesticide Safety Technical Note 18 (Bed Bugs, June 2022) and the AEPMA bed bug Code of Practice (an industry code, 4th edition), not from Mitch. What do you do with your boots, bag and gear?]

items: Note any follow-up needed and tell Mitch

sections.heading: Follow-up visit
body: Plan a follow-up visit about a week after the treatment. The spray kills the bugs but not the eggs, so anything that hatches afterwards needs treating on the follow-up. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Department of Health Pesticide Safety Technical Note 18 (Bed Bugs, June 2022), not from Mitch. When do you book it, who books it, and what does the tech do on the visit?]

sections.heading: Job complete when
items: BEFORE and AFTER photos taken
Harbourages found are treated, or noted with the reason they were not
PPE changed before the next property
Any follow-up noted and Mitch told
Anything you could not treat or reach is noted on the job report, with the reason
Product, rate, area and quantity recorded on the job report
Customer told what to do before (strip the beds, hot wash everything) and after (leave the room alone for a bit)
Customer told they can go back in once it has dried, as the product label says
Follow-up visit talked through with the customer [Mitch to confirm: timing and who books it]
Service report left, or customer told it is being emailed. Written Bed Bug Inspection report only if the customer asked for one

items.q: Can I sleep in the bed tonight?
items.a: Once it has dried, and the product label says it is OK to go back in. Then leave the room alone for a bit.

items.q: Will one visit get rid of them?
items.a: Usually not on its own. The spray kills the bugs but not the eggs, so we come back to deal with what hatches. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Department of Health Pesticide Safety Technical Note 18 (Bed Bugs, June 2022), not from Mitch]

items.q: Why do I have to hot wash everything?
items.a: Heat kills bed bugs at every stage. Wash above 60°C and dry on hot for at least 30 minutes. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Department of Health Pesticide Safety Technical Note 18 (Bed Bugs, June 2022), not from Mitch]

Some people only react to a bite days later, up to 9 to 14 days. Eggs can also hatch after the treatment, which is why we come back. [Mitch to confirm: from Victorian Department of Health Pesticide Safety Technical Note 18 (Bed Bugs, June 2022), not from Mitch]

Leave it for a bit. Too much cleaning can wipe the product off the surfaces. [Mitch to confirm: the reason is from Victorian Department of Health Pesticide Safety Technical Note 18 (Bed Bugs, June 2022), not from Mitch. How long is a bit?]

They are not known to spread disease. They can cause itching and lost sleep. If bites look infected or don't settle after a few days, see a doctor. [Mitch to confirm: from NSW Health and healthdirect, not from Mitch]

sections.heading: Tell Mitch straight away if
sections.body: Call Mitch on 0432 181 689. After hours or urgent, call Mitch directly.

items.detail: Stop immediately. Do not continue. Call Mitch.
Follow the SDS procedure. Call Mitch immediately. Never leave a spill unattended.
Treat the injury first. Call Mitch. Write down what happened.

items.text: The customer complains or gets aggressive
items.detail: Stay calm and do not argue. For a complaint, tell them Mitch will call them today. If they are aggressive, remove yourself. Call Mitch either way.

items.text: The customer asks for a quote on anything complex, or you are not sure
items.detail: Say "I'll need to get Mitch to come and have a look and provide a quote for that."

items.text: You see signs of termites or other pests outside this job
items.detail: Photograph it and tell Mitch. Termite quotes always go to Mitch.
